- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 1.1) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to avoid overshoot.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.5), model underestimates; adjust upward to reflect potential rebound.
- Model often lags behind true price movements by 1–3 days; apply a 1-day forward bias to align with sentiment-driven momentum.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model frequently overcorrects; dampen forecast slope to avoid excessive decline.
- Mean reversion is evident in 30-day horizon: if forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 1–2% to reflect diminishing momentum.
- Sentiment volatility (rapid swings) correlates with forecast error; when sentiment shifts sharply, reduce forecast confidence and apply smoother transition.
